title: Capstone Walkthrough: Marketplace Crew
objective: After this lesson you will be able to assemble a three-crew marketplace team (catalog, pricing, support) from the course's pieces, evaluate it with per-agent attribution and segment diffs, and present it as traced runs plus a findings memo — ready for the final assessment and your capstone project.
why: Nine lessons of team mechanics; one lesson of assembly. The walkthrough staffs three crews, wires delegation and boards, scopes tools, runs gold conversations, and reports per-segment truth — the complete performance your capstone repeats on its own domain. Assembly is the final team skill.

blocks.text: Catalog crew (researcher → writer → reviewer, sequential): fixed pipeline, contracted stages. Pricing crew (analyst → approver-gate, managed on signals): conditional checks, money authority gated. Support crew (triage → decide → draft → approval): the LangGraph returns graph as a subgraph, reused whole. Roster audit (Ch.2) proves pairwise partition; tool audit (Ch.7) proves least privilege; board (Ch.6) coordinates all three.

blocks.caption: Manifest-first: topologies justified, reuse explicit, eval shared

blocks.text: Catalog run: research finds specs, writer drafts, reviewer passes with two fixes — trace shows stage handoffs with contracts. Pricing run: analyst proposes, amount trips the gate, approver edits, executed — governance traced. Support run: the returns subgraph end to end with interrupt skincare. Each run: trace + key state + timing + attribution-ready slots.

Baseline per crew and overall, per-kind scores with the weakest kind named, one iterated fix with measured delta (edge examples for catalog tone misses), router coverage numbers, gate health, tool-audit result, and deferred list (fraud crew next, multilingual support later). Measured, cited, improvable — the deliverable that survives stakeholders.

blocks.title: Audit the manifest
blocks.note: Run it: expect four PASS lines then 'manifest sound'. Topology justification encoded as data: managed-with-gate, subgraph-reuse, sequential-fixed — audit the architecture before running a single agent.

items: Staff per topology-by-variability; reuse via subgraphs; audit roster + tools before running
Trace one run per crew with attribution-ready slots; findings per kind with weakest named
Memo: baselines, one iterated delta, gate health, deferred list — measured and improvable

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the manifest audit and confirm soundness. (b) Break it (remove pricing's gate) and record the audit gap — then state the real-world harm of an ungated pricing crew in one sentence. (c) Draft your capstone manifest (same shape, your domain's crews) with topology justifications per crew.
hints: Baseline sound (4 PASS); gateless pricing fails the managed-has-gate check — audits catch what enthusiasm misses.
Ungated pricing harm: autonomous money movement without approval — amounts set by agents, no human in the loop.
Your manifest needs per-crew topology + reason (fixed→sequential, variable→managed, reuse→subgraph).

exercise.why: Breakage-then-harm-statement practices audit-driven design: checks encode requirements, failures map to real incidents, manifests precede runs. Architecture audited before agents act.
exercise.code: // Manifest-audit pattern: topology requirements as runnable checks.

quiz.q: Assembly order for the marketplace team?
options: Roster + tool audits → contracts/boards → crews per topology → gold eval → one iteration — audited before acting
quiz.explain: Audit-before-act: mandates, tools, and manifests verified before runs. Assembly in dependency order with checks per arrow.

quiz.q: Pricing crew without an approval gate. Harm?
options: Autonomous money movement without human oversight — amounts set and executed by agents
quiz.explain: Money authority demands gates by value × reversibility. Ungated pricing is an incident class, not an optimization.

quiz.q: Support crew built fresh instead of reusing the returns graph. Cost?
options: Rebuilt, retested, re-debugged behavior: reuse via subgraphs with existing gold coverage beats rebuilds
quiz.explain: Reuse inherits tests, traces, and tuned prompts. Rebuilds repay all debugging already spent — subgraph composition exists precisely for this.

summary: Manifest-audited assembly, one traced run per crew, findings with per-kind truth, deferred list with reasons. Nine lessons become one operating team — assessment next, capstone after.
next: Course complete: take the 12-question final assessment (70% to pass), then ship the Marketplace Crew capstone — and step into RAG agents.
